answer: A karst survey market keeps an onchain atlas of agents. To mint identity k, its contract burns k units of a token with capped supply; one global counter assigns k and never decreases. Keys anchor reputation, and rotation preserves history. A farm with n identities burns at least n+1 tokens for its next mint. Splitting funds across wallets cannot bypass the shared counter, deletion cannot reset it, and pre-aging aliases requires every burn upfront.
